subject: On-call burst commitment checklist + policy exception request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@greenline.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-call burst commitment checklist + policy exception request

Team —

Greenline is kicking off a realtime inference pilot next week (see attached brief). They expect intermittent traffic spikes that will exceed the standard Dedicated slice limits for short windows (30–90min) during business hours. The product PM (Sara) is asking whether we can: 

- Provide a temporary autoscale exception that allows their reserved pool to burst into a shared burst lane for up to 2 hours per day for the first 2 weeks of pilot.
- Ensure we have an on-call commitment checklist (contacts, escalation path, runbook attachments) that product + Ops sign off on before the pilot starts.

I realize this touches policy and capacity — Kimberly, can you confirm whether an exception like this is feasible operationally and whether we need a formal procurement commit? Laura / Marcus — please weigh in on quota/SLAs. Sara — attaching the pilot brief and checklist that Greenline filled out.

Action items I'm proposing:
1) Kimberly: feasibility + constraints by EOD.
2) Laura: estimated additional GPU-hours and cost delta for burst windows.
3) Marcus: temporary autoscale gating (how to enforce and revert).

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Program Manager, Dedicated Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@greenline.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-call burst commitment checklist + policy exception request

Karthik —

Thanks for the note and attachments. Quick read: the request is reasonable but there are three policy points we need to clear before granting an exception: 

1) Timebox + automation: Exceptions must be timeboxed and have automation to auto-revert (we prefer feature-flagged gating). We can do 2 hours/day for 14 days if ops automation is in place.
2) Financial guardrail: We need a pre-authorized charge cap and a billing contact (to avoid surprise overages).
3) Capacity fallback: If shared burst lane is saturated, we need an agreed secondary model (smaller quantized variant) for graceful degradation.

If Greenline signs the commitment_checklist.xlsx with billing contact and fallback model, I can approve a scoped exception and prod will schedule a controlled rollout. Marcus — can you authorize the automation path (auto-revert) and define the rollback trigger?

Kimberly
Director, Dedicated Operations
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@greenline.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-call burst commitment checklist + policy exception request

Kimberly / team —

I can implement the gating via an autoscale policy override scoped to Greenline's dedicated slice. Proposed implementation notes: 
- Add time-based override (09:00–18:00 PST) that permits burst up to X GPUs (config in checklist).
- Auto-revert after 14 days or if sustained utilization > 80% for 15 minutes.
- Immediate manual rollback via the ops console (on-call playbook will include steps).

I'll prepare the runbook snippet (rollback steps + alert thresholds) and attach to the Confluence doc. Marcus

Marcus Lin
SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@greenline.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-call burst commitment checklist + policy exception request

All —

Estimate for the 14-day pilot with up to 2 hours/day burst: ~320 extra GPU-hours (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) and ballpark incremental cost of $9,600 (we'd bill per-hour per-GPU at our enterprise reserved rate). If Greenline wants a cap, we can set a hard cap on burst spend and will cut off burst automatically if the cap is reached.

Attached is a lightweight SLA matrix (ops_sla_matrix.csv) showing response times for incidents during the pilot and the billing contact field that Kimberly requested. If Greenline signs and confirms the fallback model we discussed (quantized 7B variant), we can proceed.

Laura Bennett
Billing & Capacity Planning
From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@greenline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-call burst commitment checklist + policy exception request

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Greenline is happy to: 

- Sign the commitment_checklist.xlsx and provide a billing contact (we'll return by EOD tomorrow).
- Accept the fallback to the quantized 7B model if burst lane is unavailable.
- Approve the hard cap of $10k for the 14-day pilot.

Please proceed with the automation gating and add the runbook snippet to the shared Confluence page. Once Kimberly signs the exception scope, we'll countersign and schedule the pilot kickoff.

Best,
Sara Jensen
Senior Product Manager, Greenline Health
---
Attachments referenced: pilot_brief_Greenline.pdf (pilot overview), commitment_checklist.xlsx (signed commitment fields), ops_sla_matrix.csv (SLA/billing fields)
